article_content: Pooja and Aarti Kumar, two sisters from Haryana, India, were initially hailed as national heroines after a video surfaced showing them defending themselves against men accused of sexual harassment on a public bus. Their actions, captured by a fellow passenger, sparked widespread praise and even a government offer of a cash reward. However, a newly emerged video has cast doubt on their story. In this footage, the sisters are seen initiating a physical confrontation with an unidentified man in a park. One sister grabs him by the shirt while the other strikes him with her bag. The man, appearing confused, attempts to block the blows before fleeing the scene. The sisters claim he had been verbally abusive, but the video does not clearly show this provocation. Complicating matters further, multiple passengers on the original bus have come forward with a different account. According to witness Bimla Devi, the initial conflict began when the sisters refused to vacate a seat assigned to a pregnant woman. She stated that the men merely asked them to move — a request met with resistance and escalation into physical violence. The sisters maintain that the men had touched Aarti and grabbed her throat, prompting Pooja to use her belt to strike back. They claim they were forced off the bus and escaped only after throwing a brick. Three men, reportedly trainee soldiers, were arrested but later released on bail. The bus driver and conductor were suspended for failing to report the incident. Despite the controversy, Pooja told MailOnline: 'We encounter these kinds of incidents every day. We taught them a lesson — we’re not weak. I don’t regret what we did.' The contrasting narratives have ignited a national debate on gender, self-defense, and the reliability of viral videos.

article_content: Four children were killed in a devastating house fire that broke out in rural Manitoba, Canada, on Wednesday night, despite their parents' desperate efforts to rescue them. The mother was able to pull her three youngest children—two girls and a boy—to safety, but her two older children became trapped in an upstairs bedroom and perished in the flames. The surviving children are currently staying with neighbors, as both parents are hospitalized due to smoke inhalation. The victims have been identified by Global News as 9-year-old Henry, 10-year-old Danny, 12-year-old Timmy, and 15-year-old Bobby Froese. Their mother, 34-year-old Doralee Eberhardt, was home when the fire started around midnight. Her partner, Jake Froese, and her 18-year-old son were away working a late shift. Kane Fire Chief Bernard Schellenberg said the family’s 90-year-old two-story wooden farmhouse was already fully engulfed when volunteer firefighters arrived. Due to intense heat and heavy smoke, responders could not enter the building. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police confirmed the fire began early Wednesday near the small community of Kane, approximately 60 miles southwest of Winnipeg. When Jake Froese and his eldest son returned home after midnight and saw the house ablaze, they called 911 and tried to reach the children using a ladder—but it was too late, according to a neighbor. Some 20 volunteer firefighters in four trucks arrived around 2 a.m. to find the structure completely consumed by fire. Neighbor Kristy Penner told CBC.ca she found the three youngest children crying inside a car beside their mother, while their father stood nearby, covered in soot. Doralee Eberhardt and Jake Froese are Mennonite. Some of their children were homeschooled; others attended local schools, including Lowe Farm and Rosenort schools. According to Environment Canada, temperatures in the area dropped to nearly -16°C that night. Ralph Groening, reeve of the rural community, noted that the youngest children—including a one-year-old—slept on the ground floor, while the older siblings were upstairs. Counseling services have been offered to the victims’ classmates and responding firefighters. The local community has rallied around the family, providing financial support and temporary housing.

ہوئی تو گھر میں تھیں۔ ان کا شریک، جیک فروزی، اور ان کا 18 سالہ بیٹا رات کے دیر سے شفٹ پر کام کر رہے تھے۔ کین فائر چیف برناڈ شیلنبرگ نے کہا کہ خاندان کا 90 سالہ دو منزلہ لکڑی کا گھر جب فائر فائٹرز article_content: On December 13, 2013, 68-year-old John Wise was sentenced to six years in prison for shooting his 65-year-old wife, Barbara, in her hospital bed in Akron, Ohio. He fired the gun on August 4, 2012, after witnessing her suffering following three cerebral aneurysms. Wise told authorities he acted out of compassion, unable to endure seeing his wife of 45 years in pain. He said he kissed her cheek before shooting her and then tried to take his own life—the gun jammed. Though convicted of aggravated murder and murder, the judge sentenced him under the charge of felonious assault with a firearm specification. This decision followed the prosecutor’s recommendation for leniency, even though no legal precedent existed for reducing the sentence to six years via a manslaughter charge—a charge that was never formally filed against him. Medical testimony confirmed Barbara Wise was not terminally ill but severely disabled, unable to speak, and still responding to treatment. Friends described the couple as having mutually feared a life confined to bed due to illness. John Wise himself lives with diabetes, nerve damage, and a history of bladder cancer. Under Ohio law, mercy is not a legal defense to homicide. Prosecutor Sherri Bevan Walsh called the act illegal and dangerous but urged the court to consider the unique emotional circumstances. Defense attorney Paul Adamson vowed to seek clemency from the governor regardless of the sentence.

article_content: In a historic shift for Cuba’s political landscape, President Raúl Castro has proposed imposing term limits on the nation’s highest offices — a move that could end more than half a century of rule by the Castro family. Speaking at the opening of the Communist Party’s first congress in 14 years, Castro stated that no official should hold power for more than two consecutive five-year terms, covering roles such as president and head of the Council of Ministers. His older brother, Fidel, led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until health problems forced him to step aside in 2006. Raúl, who assumed formal leadership in 2008, acknowledged that despite the urgent need for generational renewal, Cuba’s leadership has failed to cultivate a new cohort of capable successors. 'We don’t have enough qualified young people ready to step up,' he admitted, pointing to a dangerous void in leadership preparation that risks the country’s future stability.

article_content: A former SAS soldier who survived weeks of torture at the hands of Iraqi interrogators believes torture may be necessary to prevent terrorist attacks. Andy McNab, a soldier-turned-author, argues that security services have a 'moral responsibility' to interrogate suspects using physical coercion if innocent lives are at stake. A report released earlier this week revealed that brutal interrogation techniques used by CIA agents against Al-Qaeda suspects following the September 11 attacks failed to produce useful intelligence. Yet McNab contends that torture can yield critical information when applied properly—and believes authorities will continue to use it in the future to thwart terrorism. McNab, who was captured during a covert mission in the First Gulf War in January 1991, endured severe abuse: he was stripped naked, beaten, held in isolation for three weeks, whipped until he bled, and had his left molars forcibly extracted with pliers. A red-hot spoon was pressed into his open wounds. He was later transferred to Abu Ghraib, where he was beaten for another three weeks. In an interview with The Times, McNab said he 'wouldn't think twice' about inflicting pain if it could prevent an atrocity like the 2005 London bombings. 'I would deem it a moral responsibility to physically torture someone to get the information out,' he stated. 'Torture is a blunt instrument, but if used right, it can yield results.' He acknowledged that torture should occur only immediately after capture—when information is still timely—not months later, when intelligence becomes outdated. McNab conceded that while laws prohibit torture, he believes it will continue to be used covertly. 'We could moan about tactical interrogation,' he said, 'or we could moan about 24 to 28 people getting blown up on a Tube. It's a tough call.' His views contrast sharply with the findings of the US Senate Intelligence Committee, which concluded that CIA torture techniques—including waterboarding—did not produce actionable intelligence and were often ineffective and inhumane. CIA Director John Brennan has defended the agency’s past use of enhanced interrogation, claiming some information obtained saved lives, though he admitted agents used 'unauthorized methods.' Despite enduring extreme suffering himself, McNab maintains that torture is 'a weapon misunderstood by those who were neither inflicting nor experiencing it.' He argues that moral revulsion fades when real-time intelligence could prevent mass casualties.
translated_content: ایک سابقہ ایس اے ایس فوجی جس نے عراقی تفتیش کاروں کے ہاتھوں ہفتوں تک تعذیب سے جان بچائی، سمجھتا ہے کہ دہشت گردی کے حملوں کو روکنے کے لیے تعذیب ضروری ہو سکتی ہے۔ اینڈی مک نیب، ایک فوجی جو مصنف بن گیا، کہتے ہیں کہ اگر بے گناہ زندگیاں خطرے میں ہوں تو محفوظ خدمات کو 'اخلاقی ذمہ داری' ہے کہ وہ مشتبہ کو جسمانی زبردستی کے ذریعے پوچھ گچھ کریں۔ اس ہفتے شائع ہونے والی ایک رپورٹ نے ظاہر کیا کہ سی آئی اے کے ایجنسٹوں نے سیپٹمبر 11 کے حملوں کے بعد القاعدہ کے مشتبہوں کے خلاف جبری طریقے استعمال کیے، جن سے مفید معلومات حاصل نہیں ہو سکیں۔ لیکن مک نیب کا دعویٰ ہے کہ اگر صحیح طریقے سے استعمال کیا جائے تو تعذیب اہم معلومات فراہم کر سکتی ہے—اور وہ سمجھتے ہیں کہ مستقبل میں افسران دہشت گردی کو روکنے کے لیے اس کا استعمال جاری رکھیں گے۔ مک نیب، جنہیں جنگ فارس کے دوران جنوری 1991 میں ایک چھپے ہوئے مشن کے دوران گرفتار کیا گیا تھا، انہوں نے شدید زیادتی برداشت کی: انہیں ننگا کر دیا گیا، پیٹا گیا، تین ہفتوں تک تنہا رکھا گیا، ان کو چھڑیوں سے چھڑیا گیا کہ خون بہنے لگا، اور ان کے بائیں طرف کے ٹیکسے پلائرز سے نکال دیے گئے۔ ان کے کھلے زخموں میں ایک گرم دھاتی چمچ دبا دی گئی۔ بعد میں انہیں ابو غریب میں منتقل کر دیا گیا، جہاں انہیں مزید تین ہفتوں تک پیٹا گیا۔ ٹائمز کے ساتھ ایک انٹرویو میں، مک نیب نے کہا کہ اگر وہ کسی برے عمل کو روک سکتے ہوں تو وہ 'دونوں کو سوچے بغیر' درد پہنچائیں گے، جیسا کہ 2005 کے لندن بم دھماکے۔ انہوں نے کہا: 'میں اس شخص سے معلومات نکالنے کے لیے جسمانی تعذیب کرنے کو اخلاقی ذمہ داری سمجھوں گا۔' 'تعذیب ایک خشن آلہ ہے، لیکن اگر صحیح طریقے سے استعمال کیا جائے تو نتائج دے سکتی ہے۔' انہوں نے تسلیم کیا کہ تعذیب صرف گرفتاری کے فوراً بعد ہی کی جانی چاہیے—جب معلومات ابھی تازہ ہوں—نہ کہ ماہوں بعد جب معلومات 'قدیم' ہو جائیں۔ مک نیب نے تسلیم کیا کہ جبکہ قانون تعذیب کو منع کرتا ہے، وہ سمجھتے ہیں کہ اسے چھپا کر جاری رکھا جائے گا۔ 'ہم تاکتی تفتیش کے بارے میں شکایت کر سکتے ہیں،' انہوں نے کہا، 'یا ہم ٹیوب میں 24 سے 28 افراد کے پھٹ جانے کے بارے میں شکایت کر سکتے ہیں۔ یہ ایک مشکل فیصلہ ہے۔' ان کے خیالات امریکی سینیٹ کی معلوماتی کمیٹی کی تحقیقات سے واضح طور پر متضاد ہیں، جس نے نتیجہ اخذ کیا کہ سی آئی اے کے تعذیب کے طریقے—جس میں واٹر بورڈنگ شامل ہے—کوئی عملی معلومات نہیں دے سکے اور یہ اکثر ناکارہ اور لا انسانی تھے۔ سی آئی اے کے ڈائریکٹر جان برینن نے ایجنسی کے گزشتہ تعذیب article_content: Hamed Arbabi, the founder and CEO of VoPay, is a respected voice in global fintech—but his insights aren’t just for specialists anymore. Today, even airlines sell Wi-Fi, car lenders offer insurance, and subscription apps handle payments. Why? Because the line between tech and finance is vanishing. Companies no longer need to be banks to deliver financial services—they just need to embed them. Over the past two years, awareness of embedded payments has exploded across North America. By 2026, B2B embedded payment platforms are expected to generate nearly $7 billion, up from under $2 billion in 2021. Businesses are under pressure: 84% of leaders fear economic headwinds, and 90% of CFOs admit their teams are bogged down by manual payment tasks. Paper checks? Still around—and their fraud rates have doubled. That’s why smarter systems are stepping in. Embedded payments replace risky data with secure tokens, detect fraud in real time, and slash processing times by up to 16 days, according to PYMNTS. For customers, this means paying when they want, how they want—via card, wallet, or bank transfer—all within the app they’re already using. But it’s not easy. Integrating payments without breaking the user experience requires deep technical planning. Supporting dozens of local payment methods, ensuring system compatibility, and training staff are all hurdles. Get it wrong, and users leave. Get it right, and you turn a simple transaction into a revenue engine—unlocking upsells, subscriptions, and loyalty loops. The future isn’t about becoming a bank. It’s about letting your platform become the invisible financial backbone of your customers’ lives. And in uncertain times, that’s not just smart—it’s survival.

article_content: New York (CNN) — A 25-year-old man has been charged with trespassing after jumping from the Bronx Zoo’s Wild Asia monorail into a tiger enclosure, saying he wanted to 'be one' with the animal, police said Saturday. David Villalobos, who is currently hospitalized in stable condition, told authorities his leap was not a suicide attempt, but a deliberate effort to connect with the tiger, according to NYPD spokesman Paul Browne. The incident occurred around 3 p.m. Friday, when Villalobos exited the moving monorail car and cleared the exhibit’s perimeter fence, landing inside the Tiger Mountain habitat, said Bronx Zoo Director Jim Breheny. Villalobos suffered multiple serious injuries — including a broken right shoulder, rib, ankle, and pelvis, a collapsed lung, and puncture wounds — according to NYPD spokesperson Brian Sessa. He later reported petting one of the tigers before it retreated. Zoo responders used a fire extinguisher to distract the tiger, prompting Villalobos to follow instructions and roll under an electric 'hot wire' — a low-voltage deterrent designed to discourage animals from approaching restricted zones. Breheny said the action likely saved his life. The tiger, which had ample opportunity to attack, instead backed away. 'If the tiger really wanted to do harm, it certainly had the time,' Breheny told reporters. 'This is an extraordinary occurrence caused by someone deliberately putting themselves in danger.' Villalobos was conscious and speaking as he was transported to Jacobi Medical Center in the Bronx. He faces charges of trespassing and criminal trespassing; an arraignment date has not yet been scheduled. Tiger Mountain, home to Siberian and Malayan tigers, is part of the Bronx Zoo — New York City’s flagship wildlife park operated by the Wildlife Conservation Society.
translated_content: نیو یارک (سی این این) — ایک 25 سالہ مرد کو برونکس زو کے وائلڈ ایشیا مونوریل سے کود کر شیر کے گھر میں داخل ہونے پر گھسٹنے کا الزام لگایا گیا، جس نے کہا کہ وہ جانور کے ساتھ 'ایک' بننا چاہتا تھا، پولیس نے جمعہ کو کہا۔ ڈیوڈ ویلالوبوس، جو اب استحکام کی حالت میں ہسپتال میں ہیں، نے افسر کو بتایا کہ ان کی کوشش خودکشی کا مقصود نہیں تھی، بلکہ شیر کے ساتھ جڑنے کی ارادہ سے کی گئی تھی، جس کی تصدیق ایم یو پی ڈی کے ترجمان پال برون نے کی۔ حادثہ جمعہ کو تقریباً 3 بجے ہوا، جب ویلالوبوس نے چلنے والے مونوریل کار سے کود کر ایکسہبٹ کی گرد دیوار عبور کر کے ٹائجر ماؤنٹن کے اندر اتر گئے، جس کی تفصیل برونکس زو کے ڈائریکٹر جم بیرینی نے دی۔ ویلالوبوس کو متعدد شدید زخموں کا شکار ہوا — جن میں دائیں کندھے، پلیٹ، اور ٹھوڑی کی ٹوٹ، ایک جھٹکا لگا، اور چھیڑ چھاڑ کے زخم شامل ہیں، جیسا کہ ایم یو پی ڈی کے ترجمان برائن سیسا نے بتایا۔ انہوں نے بعد میں دعویٰ کیا کہ انہوں نے ایک شیر کو چھوا، جس کے بعد وہ پیچھے ہٹ گیا۔ زوب کے مددگاروں نے شیر کو الگ کرنے کے لیے ایک فائر ایکسٹنگوئشر کا استعمال کیا، جس سے ویلالوبوس نے ہدایات کی پیروی کرتے ہوئے ایک بجلی والا 'ہاٹ وائر' کے نیچے لپکنا شروع کر دیا — جو جانوروں کو محدود علاقوں کی طرف آنے سے روکنے کے لیے ڈیزائن کیا گیا ہے۔ بیرینی نے کہا کہ یہ کارروائی اس کی زندگی بچانے کا سبب بن سکی۔ شیر، جس کے پاس حملہ کرنے کا کافی وقت تھا، اس نے پیچھے ہٹ دیا۔ 'اگر شیر حقیقت میں اس شخص کو نقصان پہنچانا چاہتا تھا تو وہ بالکل اس کا وقت رکھتا تھا،' بیرینی نے رپورٹرز کو بتایا۔ 'یہ ایک غیر معمولی واقعہ ہے جو اس لیے پیش آیا کہ کسی نے جان بوجھ کر خود کو خطرے میں ڈالا۔' ویلالوبوس کو جب ہسپتال منتقل کیا گیا تو وہ آگے بات کر رہے تھے۔ ان پر گھسٹنے اور جرمی گھسٹنے کا الزام لگایا گیا ہے؛ ابھی تک کوئی عدالتی سننے کی تاریخ مقرر نہیں ہوئی ہے۔ ٹائجر ماؤنٹن، جس میں سائبیرین اور ملائیشیائی شیر رہتے ہیں، برونکس زو کا حصہ ہے — جو نیو یارک شہر کا اہم جانوروں کا پارک ہے اور وائلڈ لائف کنسرویشن سوسائٹی کے تحت چلایا جاتا ہے۔

article_content: By Phil Vinter. PUBLISHED: 11:57 EST, 14 July 2012. | UPDATED: 12:21 EST, 14 July 2012. A jealous husband who shot his wife five times with an illegal firearm after learning of her secret affair with a younger man has been jailed for 12 years. David Leeman, 60, shot Jennie Leeman, 44, with a semi-automatic pistol at close range in a barn on their former farm in rural Devon. Their marriage had deteriorated over 20 years, during which they had two sons and two daughters, when Mrs. Leeman began an affair with Norman Laramy, 40. At Exeter Crown Court, jurors heard that Leeman discovered the affair six days before the killing. He claimed he heard voices and lost control due to antidepressant medication, leading him to plead guilty to manslaughter. However, senior medical experts were divided on whether his dosage could have impaired his judgment. The jury acquitted Leeman of murder after nine and a half hours of deliberation but found him guilty of manslaughter. The prosecution argued he planned the attack: he retrieved the gun, cleaned it, loaded it, and concealed it before confronting his wife. Passing sentence, Mr Justice Butterfield said he was 'wholly unimpressed' by claims of diminished responsibility. 'You were not out of control when you recovered the gun, cleaned it, or placed it in your pocket,' he stated. 'You took out the loaded gun and pointed it at her. You were not out of control—even though you were emotionally overwhelmed.' The judge noted that Jennie laughed at Leeman’s threats, triggering the fatal shooting. 'You acted out of anger and frustration, not fear. Your intention was to kill her.' Leeman had no prior violent convictions and expressed remorse, telling police, 'I shot the woman I loved because she didn't do what I wanted.' He also said he recited the Lord’s Prayer over her body before attempting suicide with an empty gun. The judge sentenced him to 12 years for manslaughter and five years for illegal firearm possession, to run concurrently. With 296 days already served, he will serve half the sentence in prison before release on license. Defense counsel Martin Meeke QC emphasized Leeman’s genuine remorse and his stated desire to join his wife in death. But Jennie’s family expressed disappointment, stating: 'No one has the right to take another person’s life. Justice has not been done for our wonderful daughter, sister, and friend.'

سے باہر نہیں تھے،' اس نے کہا۔ 'آپ نے لوڈ شدہ گن نکالی اور اسے اس کی طرف اشارہ کیا۔ آپ کنٹرول سے باہر نہیں تھے—اگرچہ آپ ایک جذباتی طور پر بہت تشدد میں تھے۔' جج نے نوٹ کیا کہ جینی نے لیمن کے دھمکیوں پر کیا، پولیس کو بتایا، 'میں نے اس عورت کو گولی مار دی جسے میں پیار کرتا تھا کیونکہ اس نے مجھے جو چاہا وہ نہیں کیا۔' اس نے اس کے جسم پر رب کی دعا پڑھی اور خودکشی کی کوشش کی، لیکن گن میں کوئی گولی نہیں تھی۔ جج نے اسے قتل کے لیے 12 سال اور غیر قانونی ہتھیار رکھنے کے لیے پانچ سال کی سزا سنائی، جو ایک ساتھ چلیں گی۔ 296 دن پہلے سے قید میں گزار چکا ہے، اس کی سزا کا آدھا حصہ جیل میں گزارنے کے بعد لائسنس پر جاری ہو جائے گا۔ دفاعی وکیل مارٹن میک کے نے لیمن کے اصل افسوس اور اپنی بیوی کے ساتھ مرنے کی خواہش پر زور دیا۔ لیکن جینی کے خاندان نے نااخلاقیت کا اظہار کیا، کہتے ہوئے: 'کسی کے پاس دوسرے کی زندگی لینے کا کوئی حق نہیں ہے۔ ہم، جینی کے خاندان، ناامید ہیں اور ڈیوڈ لیمن نے ہماری عزیز بیٹی، بہن اور بہت سے لوگوں کے دوست کے ساتھ جو بہت برا کیا، اس کے لیے انصاف نہیں ہوا۔'

article_content: A 15-year-old British schoolgirl, Yusra Hussien, has disappeared after traveling from Bristol to Istanbul, reportedly to join ISIS in Syria. She is believed to have been radicalized through online jihadist propaganda. Described as an outstanding student with aspirations to become a dentist, Yusra left home last Wednesday without informing her family. She is thought to have boarded a flight to Istanbul alongside another teenage girl from South London. Counter-extremism expert Haras Rafiq of the Quilliam Foundation warns that Yusra may be groomed into becoming a so-called 'jihadi bride'—a role often imposed on young women by ISIS recruiters, who encourage them to marry fighters as a form of service to the group. Her family, of Somali heritage, are devastated and have publicly pleaded for her return. They say they had no knowledge of her plans and believe she was influenced solely through internet exposure. Police have confirmed they are tracing her movements but have not explained how she passed through Heathrow’s security without parental authorization. The airline and travel details remain undisclosed. Yusra’s case is not isolated: up to 50 British girls and young women are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS, some as young as 14. Several have reportedly married fighters or taken on domestic roles within militant communities. Experts stress that radicalization often occurs in isolation through encrypted forums and social media—not through formal institutions—and that many families remain unaware until it is too late. Avon and Somerset Police urge the public to recognize warning signs of radicalization, such as sudden changes in behavior, increased secrecy around device use, or expressions of extremist ideology. ISIS has no legitimacy in Islam, and its actions are condemned by Muslim communities worldwide. The focus must remain on prevention, protection, and rehabilitation—not stigma.

article_content: During their debut joint appearance on The View, Barack and Michelle Obama opened up about the simple, heartfelt routines that keep their family connected. Michelle joked that she’s too impatient for politics — a clear no to any future presidential run — while revealing how Barack tucks her in every night after putting their daughters to bed. 'They yell, 'I wanna be tucked!' and then he turns off the lights and we chat,' she said. 'He asks, 'Ready to be tucked?' It’s our thing.' Barack reflected on their nearly 20-year marriage, saying their bond has grown deeper since moving into the White House. 'I live above the store,' he quipped, noting his 30-second commute makes dinner together easier. 'After two decades, trust isn’t just built — it’s engraved.' He shared that Malia, now 14, has become a night owl just like him. 'They still love their dad — but they visit strategically. Five minutes, then they’re gone.' Before delivering his keynote at the 2012 Democratic National Convention, he saw Malia and Sasha spinning around backstage. 'It hit me — this is exactly like Hannah Montana when Billy Ray tells her, 'Go get ‘em, baby!' I walked out thinking about that. Honestly, that’s what calmed me down.' When the girls walk Bo after dinner, Barack and Michelle steal quiet moments to talk about real life — the kind of heavy stuff Michelle is glad she doesn’t have to handle directly. 'I have the best job,' she said. 'Hula-hooping. Meeting amazing people. I don’t know how he does it.' Asked about life after the presidency, Obama said he dreams of mentoring young people across the country — not necessarily in classrooms, but through apprenticeships and community programs. 'I miss teaching. I want to help kids see their own potential.' He also gently nudged Michelle to consider office, saying she’d be 'terrific' — though she firmly replied, 'It takes patience I just don’t have.'

خواب دیکھتے ہیں — بالکل کلاس روم میں نہیں، بلکہ ملازمتوں اور کمیونٹی پروگراموں کے ذریعے۔ 'میں تدریس کی یاد کرتا ہوں۔ میں چاہتا ہوں کہ بچوں کو اپنی صلاحیت دیکھنے میں مدد کروں۔' انہوں نے میشل کو عہدے کے article_content: For many Australians, the supermarket experience feels like a nightmare: long checkout lines, empty shelves, screaming children, and trolleys blocking the aisles. A national survey of 2,500 consumers reveals that 62% consider endless checkout queues their biggest pet peeve. More than half of respondents were frustrated to find their favorite items out of stock. Additionally, 35% expressed dissatisfaction when their preferred brands were replaced by supermarket private-label products. Other major annoyances included unruly children (38%), self-checkout malfunctions (38%), and trolleys obstructing pathways (36%). Finding a parking spot before shopping even began was a major hassle for 28%, while difficulty locating staff for help ranked equally high. On the lighter side, 11% found overly friendly cashiers to be a minor nuisance, and only 8% were bothered by the absence of alcohol sales in supermarkets. Shockingly, 8% admitted to having stolen something — either by not scanning items at self-checkout or walking out without paying. Canstar Blue, which conducted the survey, noted these frustrations are entirely understandable. Spokesman Simon Downes explained, 'If you’ve already battled parking, crowded aisles, and sold-out items, the last thing you want is to wait ten minutes to pay.' Meanwhile, 74% of Australians prioritize buying locally produced food. A strong majority — 68% — say they’re comfortable eating food a day or two past its 'use by' date, and 65% believe their supermarket offers the best value. Despite 46% thinking they could save money elsewhere, 53% remain loyal to their current store for its convenience. Advertising has little impact: only 13% have switched supermarkets because of a TV ad, and just 8% care if a celebrity chef endorses a chain. In short, Australians want speed, reliability, and respect for their time — not small talk, stockouts, or parking nightmares.

درصد از کارکنان صرافی بسیار دوستانه، کمی ناراحت‌کننده بودند و تنها ۸ درصد از عدم موجود بودن الکل در فروشگاه‌های مواد غذایی ناراضی بودند. شگفت‌آور است که ۸ درصد اعتراف کردند که چیزی دزدیده‌اند — یا با عدم اسکن کردن محصولات در خودپرداز یا بدون پرداخت از فروشگاه بیرون رفته‌اند. کانستار بلو، که این نظرسنجی را انجام داده، این ناراحتی‌ها را کاملاً قابل درک می‌داند. سخنگوی آن، سایمون داونز، توضیح داد: 'اگر شما قبلاً با پارکینگ، راه‌های پر از مردم و محصولات تمام شده مبارزه کرده‌اید، آخرین چیزی که می‌خواهید ده دقیقه در صف منتظر بمانید.' در عین حال، ۷۴ درصد استرالیایی‌ها ترجیح می‌دهند غذاهای تولید داخلی بخرند. اکثریت قاطع — ۶۸ درصد — می‌گویند که خوردن محصولات یک یا دو روز پس از تاریخ مصرف آن‌ها برایشان مشکلی ندارد و ۶۵ درصد معتقدند فروشگاهشان بهترین ارزش را ارائه می‌دهد. با وجود اینکه ۴۶ درصد فکر می‌کنند می‌توانند جای دیگری ارزان‌تر بخرند، ۵۳ درصد به دلیل راحتی، به فروشگاه فعلی خود وفادار می‌مانند. تبلیغات تأثیر کمی دارد: فقط ۱۳ درصد به دلیل تبلیغات تلویزیونی فروشگاه را عوض کرده‌اند و تنها ۸ درصد به این موضوع که یک سرشناس آشپز به یک فروشگاه وابسته شده است، اهمیت می‌دهند. به طور خلاصه، استرالیایی‌ها به سرعت، قابلیت اطمینان و احترام به زمانشان نیاز دارند — نه گفتگوهای کوچک، نه کمبود کالا article_content: UEFA has raised serious concerns that FIFA’s legal team may be editing the Michael Garcia report on World Cup bidding corruption to shield former president Sepp Blatter. These fears follow revelations from Germany’s Der Spiegel that key criticisms of Blatter in last year’s reform report by Mark Pieth were quietly removed by Zurich-based lawyer Marco Villiger. Michel Platini, head of UEFA, called the interference 'blatant' and said it confirms long-standing doubts about FIFA’s so-called independent governance committee. He added that UEFA’s own efforts to push for reform had been unfairly blamed — now, the motive behind those accusations seems clearer. Garcia’s surprise resignation from his investigator role may have less to do with controversies surrounding Russia or Qatar and more with his findings on Blatter being softened or erased. Prince Ali of Jordan echoed these concerns, stating that without releasing the full Garcia report, FIFA will continue to face public distrust. In response, FIFA insists only five minor, procedural edits were made and denies any attempt to manipulate the outcome. Meanwhile, in English football, Aston Villa owner Randy Lerner continues to send mixed signals about selling the club — even as he spends much of his time relaxing at the Sandy Lane resort in Barbados instead of attending matches. At Channel 4, plans to have reality TV host Jeremy Kyle anchor the Grand National coverage have been scrapped; the network is returning to its regular racing presenter, Nick Luck, following Clare Balding’s decision to cover the Boat Race for the BBC. At Leicester City, tensions are high between manager Nigel Pearson and director of football Jon Rudkin, a close ally of the club’s Thai owners. Their strained relationship, dating back to a prior fallout, has deepened the club’s instability — especially after Pearson was briefly sacked and then reinstated over the weekend. Rudkin, formerly the academy director, has largely stayed out of Pearson’s way since taking over last December. In broadcasting, the Premier League’s £4 billion TV rights auction enters its second round, with BT and Sky as the top contenders. While Sky is expected to keep its prized 4pm Sunday slot, BT could secure up to 56 of the 168 live matches per season — roughly doubling its current haul. The average cost per game is projected to hit £8 million. The FA is frustrated by FIFA’s latest moves: banning third-party player ownership and shifting agent regulation back to national federations — all without offering practical guidance on implementation. This follows FIFA’s rejection of emergency loans between clubs, despite support from both its own executive and the English football community. Finally, England’s Women’s Cricket Team sparked online mockery after posing in elegant ball gowns for a Waitrose-sponsored shoot at Lord’s Long Room. The intended 'Downton Abbey' aesthetic backfired after Piers Morgan, a vocal supporter of Kevin Pietersen, led a viral campaign labeling it 'Downton Shabby,' targeting England cricket chief Paul Downton.

article_content: In August 2010, federal inspectors uncovered horrifying conditions at several major egg-producing farms in Iowa, triggering one of the largest food safety recalls in U.S. history — over half a billion eggs pulled from shelves due to salmonella contamination. The FDA’s findings at six farms operated by Wright County Egg and Quality Egg, along with three Hillandale Farms sites, painted a grim picture: towering piles of chicken manure up to eight feet high, rodents entering through gaps blocked by waste, flies so numerous they were uncountable, and uncaged hens wading through feces to reach laying areas. Investigators confirmed salmonella in chicken feed, barn flooring, and — critically — in the water used to wash eggs at one Hillandale facility. Although new federal egg safety rules went into effect in mid-July 2010, none of the companies had effectively implemented their required salmonella prevention plans. Workers frequently failed to wear protective clothing, feed bins were corroded and leaking, and maggot-infested zones were widespread. The Center for Science in the Public Interest labeled the conditions 'stomach-churning,' accusing the firms of ignoring safety mandates for over a year despite repeated warnings. Both Wright County Egg and Hillandale claimed they had begun correcting issues before or during the inspections, with some fixes made on the spot. However, consumer advocates argue these delays reflect systemic negligence enabled by infrequent oversight. In response, the FDA pledged to inspect all 600 regulated egg facilities across the U.S. within the next 15 months. Siobhan DeLancey, an FDA spokesperson, clarified that the reports were preliminary observations and did not constitute formal enforcement actions. Future inspections will target farms based on size, egg output, violation history, and links to past outbreaks. Hillandale denied being singled out, stating it had developed specific action plans to resolve every issue raised. Wright County Egg asserted that nearly all violations had been or would be resolved by mid-September. Yet, the revelations have severely shaken public confidence in industrial egg production — raising urgent questions about the effectiveness of regulatory oversight.

article_content: Even after being told he had only months to live, Sam Simon — the brilliant mind behind The Simpsons — chose not to retreat into sorrow, but to embrace life with laughter and generosity. Diagnosed with advanced colon cancer two years ago, Simon recalls doctors showing him scans they described as those of a dying man. When he asked if it was curable, the response was blunt: 'We don’t use that word.' Yet, through persistent treatment and unwavering support, he’s defied expectations. Today, he says he’s never felt happier. Much of that joy, he explains, comes from being surrounded by loved ones who care deeply for him. But his true legacy is taking shape through action: he’s committed to giving away his entire fortune — estimated from decades in Hollywood, including hits like Taxi and Cheers — to help animals and feed the hungry. Working closely with PETA founder Ingrid Newkirk, Simon helps plan and participate in animal rescue missions that bring him purpose. Through his Sam Simon Foundation, he ensures 400 Los Angeles families receive meals every single day. 'I feel responsible,' he says, 'to speak for those who can’t speak for themselves.' Though he admits cancer is brutal and he still struggles, he calls this chapter the most profound, enlightening, and even beautiful experience of his life.

article_content: Andy Robertson has firmly pushed back against suggestions that Scotland will resort to physical play when they face England in Glasgow on Tuesday. The match, the first between the two rivals in the Scottish capital since their dramatic 1999 Euro 2000 playoff clash, comes on the back of Scotland’s 1-0 victory over the Republic of Ireland — sealed by a stunning goal from Shaun Maloney at Celtic Park. While England’s upcoming goalkeeper Ben Foster remarked that Scotland and Ireland had been ‘kicking lumps out of each other’ during their recent encounter, Robertson dismissed the comment as merely an opinion. ‘That’s his take,’ he said. ‘We were out there playing football. Look at the goal — pure technique, straight off the training pitch, and Shaun’s finish? Unbelievable.’ The 20-year-old left-back admits he doesn’t recall Paul Scholes’ brace in the 1999 match at Hampden Park — he was just five years old — but he did watch England’s 2012 friendly win at Wembley while living in Dundee after signing for Dundee United. Though he grew up during a time when the Scotland-England fixture had lost some of its former intensity, Robertson knows its significance. ‘It was always something we heard about,’ he said. ‘It’ll be a fierce game — but one played with quality, not just force.’

article_content: On July 24, 2012, Queen Elizabeth II hosted a rare Diamond Jubilee lunch at 10 Downing Street, joined by four of her former Prime Ministers: David Cameron, Sir John Major, Tony Blair, and Gordon Brown. The gathering marked a historic moment — only the sixth time in her reign that a sitting Prime Minister had invited her to the official residence. The Queen, known for her private weekly meetings with each Prime Minister over the decades — totalling 538 hours, according to Mr. Cameron — reportedly shares deeper personal connections with them than they do with each other. Only Baroness Thatcher, due to poor health, was absent. While political differences were set aside for the occasion, aides quietly acknowledged the complexity of seating arrangements, placing Cabinet Secretary Sir Jeremy Heywood and Deputy PM Nick Clegg as buffers to ease tensions — especially given Gordon Brown’s strained history with both Blair and Clegg. Brown was seated between Dame Norma Major and Sir Jeremy. The Queen was flanked by David Cameron and Sir John Major. Guests included Samantha Cameron and Miriam Gonzalez Durantez. The meal featured salmon, roast duck breast with seasonal vegetables, and trifle. A noticeable fashion coincidence emerged: both the Queen and Samantha Cameron wore nearly identical blue-and-white digital-print dresses. While Mrs. Cameron’s £495 Jonathan Saunders gown drew public praise, the Queen’s expression remained composed yet distant — widely interpreted as displeasure. Clarence House later clarified that there are no official dress codes for meeting the Queen, nor is her attire ever disclosed in advance. This rare visit underscored the Queen’s enduring symbolic role — bridging political eras while navigating unspoken protocols, even in moments of unintended social missteps.

article_content: Judge Lindsey Kushner QC said Stefu Costel lent his nation a bad name at Manchester Crown Court. A judge has condemned a Romanian man who stole 27 smartphones worth £9,000 from Limp Bizkit fans at a concert in Manchester, telling him: 'We do not want criminals such as yourself in this country.' Police raided Costel’s flat in Chorlton, Manchester, and found 27 handsets stuffed inside a plastic carrier bag. All had been stolen from concertgoers during a performance by the American nu-metal band Limp Bizkit at The Academy on Oxford Road in February. Costel, 30, originally from Romania, claimed he was asked by his brother’s friend to hold onto the bag, but pleaded guilty to handling stolen goods and was jailed for 14 months. Judge Kushner described the thefts as part of an 'absolute plague' across the UK, stating: 'It lends his nation a bad name. Everybody gets tarred with the same brush. He is one of those people in one of those gangs who go to public events and sweep through everyone. These are offences that are a plague on all of us. It is not just petty pickpocketing—it is organized gang theft, and you are part of that arrangement.' Costel, who lived at Railway Terrace in Chorlton, previously served time for stealing phones from music fans at the Reading Festival and had a prior conviction for conspiring to steal from bank customers using debit and credit card fraud. Prosecutor Tim Greenald told the court that most victims—mostly men—did not realize their phones had been taken until later that night. The stolen devices included iPhones, Samsung Galaxy phones, HTC phones, and Sony Xperia phones. The thefts were organized and likely involved multiple skilled individuals. All 27 phones will be returned to their owners. Costel denied knowing the bag contained phones and claimed no financial benefit. Police conducted the raid at his home just two days after the concert thefts. Defender Nicola Gatto stated that Costel suffers from an acute psychotic disorder and wishes to return to Romania.

فروری میں مینچسٹر کے آکسفورڈ روڈ پر واقع دی اکیڈمی میں امریکی نیو میٹل بینڈ لمپ بزکٹ کے کنسٹ میں فینز سے چوری کیے گئے تھے۔ کوسیل، جو 30 سال کا ہے اور اصل میں رومانیہ سے ہے، نے دعویٰ کیا کہ اس کے بھائی کے لیے ایک طاعون ہیں۔ یہ صرف چھیننے کا ایک چھوٹا سا معاملہ نہیں ہے — یہ منظم گینگ چوری ہے، اور آپ اس سازش کا حصہ ہیں۔' کوسیل، جو وقتاً فوقتاً چورلٹن کے ریلوے ٹیریس میں رہتا تھا، پہلے بھی ریڈنگ فیسٹیول متاثرین — زیادہ تر مرد — کو جب یہ واقعہ ہوا تو انہیں پتہ نہیں چلا کہ ان کے فون چوری ہو گئے ہیں، لیکن رات کے دوران انہیں احساس ہوا کہ وہ شکار بن گئے ہیں۔ چوری شدہ ہینڈ سیٹس میں آئی فون، سیم سنگ گلیکسی، article_content: As tensions rise across the region, numerous global airlines have suspended or adjusted flights to Israel amid growing security concerns. Virgin Atlantic has cancelled eight round-trip flights between London Heathrow and Tel Aviv from Saturday through next Wednesday, citing passenger safety as its top priority. British Airways has shifted its daily Tel Aviv departures from afternoon to morning to avoid overnight stays by crew members, while also introducing a flexible booking policy allowing free date changes. Wizz Air has halted all Tel Aviv services indefinitely, and EasyJet paused operations over the weekend, planning further schedule adjustments for the week ahead. Major international carriers including Emirates, Lufthansa, and Air France have also suspended flights to Israel. In the United States, United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and American Airlines announced the temporary suspension of direct routes, with United stating flights will remain paused 'until conditions allow them to resume' and Delta confirming cancellations extend through the current week. Hamas claimed responsibility for targeting Ben Gurion International Airport with missile strikes on Monday, contributing to the heightened risk assessment. Since the outbreak of violence on Saturday, more than 700 people have been killed in Israel, and approximately 500 others in Gaza due to retaliatory airstrikes. The UK Foreign Office now advises against all non-essential travel to Israel and the Occupied Palestinian Territories, and warns against any travel to specific high-risk zones. Meanwhile, Poland and Hungary have successfully evacuated around 300 citizens via special flights, with Thailand and Nepal reportedly evaluating similar efforts. Royal Caribbean is revising cruise itineraries in the region and contacting affected passengers. The Association of British Travel Agents recommends that package holidaymakers contact their tour operators for options including refunds, rescheduling, or alternative destinations. Independent travelers are urged to consult their airlines and accommodation providers directly. Despite widespread cancellations, some flights—such as those operated by Ryanair and Pegasus—continued operating into Monday morning, though Ryanair later confirmed it too had cancelled multiple flights and urged passengers to verify real-time updates.

article_content: In the wake of a devastating October 2013 blizzard across South Dakota, thousands of cattle perished—many frozen in place, others carried miles away by ferocious winds. Estimates suggest up to 20,000 animals died, leaving ranchers grappling with unimaginable losses. The snowstorm, which dumped over 30 inches in parts of the Black Hills, turned once-familiar pastures into grim landscapes littered with bloated, blackened carcasses. Cleanup crews began the grim task of removing the dead, but for many farmers, the damage was already irreversible. Ranchers described the event as the worst livestock disaster they’d ever witnessed. Karl Knutson, a 25-year-old rancher near Sturgis, counted his losses while others, like Gary Cammack of Union Center, lost roughly 15% of their herd—about 70 adult cows and calves. Each animal represented thousands of dollars in income: calves worth around $1,000, mature cows closer to $1,500 or more. 'It’s bad. It’s really bad,' Cammack said, despite his typically optimistic outlook. State veterinarian Dustin Oedekoven noted the randomness of survival: some ranchers lost half their herds, others none at all. 'There was no rhyme or reason,' he said. Meanwhile, dozens of cattle had been blown far beyond fences, scattered across remote terrain. Alan Rislov, near Philip, suspected hundreds of his animals were missing—and possibly dead—but couldn’t confirm until search efforts concluded. Adding to the crisis, no federal disaster program currently exists to help. The last one expired at the end of 2011. Although both the House and Senate had proposed livestock aid in their respective farm bills—covering 75% and 65% of market value respectively—no final agreement had been reached. Senator John Thune urged lawmakers to act, saying the tragedy might finally push Congress to pass a long-stalled bill. For now, ranchers were left to pick up the pieces alone.

article_content: Capturing panoramic shots used to mean awkwardly spinning in circles with your phone — but not anymore. Ricoh, a Japanese tech company, has introduced the Theta, the world’s first handheld camera that snaps a complete 360-degree photo with just one press of a button. Inside, a sleek twin-lens system captures everything around you — above, below, and all sides — instantly stitching it into a seamless spherical image. Weighing only 95 grams and fitting neatly in your palm like a remote, the Theta is built for simplicity. The shutter button sits right beneath the lenses, so you can trigger the shot with your thumb without fumbling. There’s no screen on the device itself — instead, photos automatically sync to your smartphone or tablet via Wi-Fi, letting you rotate, zoom, and explore the full scene on your mobile screen. While basic cropping is possible on your phone, advanced editing tools are minimal. Once you’re happy with the shot, you can upload it to Ricoh’s theta360.com platform and share it directly to Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, or Microsoft’s Photosynth. Launching in October for £329, the Theta will be available for pre-order in the UK, US, Germany, and France. Initially, it works with iPhones 4S and 5 running iOS 6.0 or higher, plus the free Ricoh Theta app from the App Store. Android compatibility is expected before the year ends. Ricoh’s leadership sees the Theta as more than a gadget — it’s a tool to help people see the world differently. ‘It captures everything in one frame,’ says Wataru Ohtani, ‘revealing how we’re all connected.’ President Noboru Akahane adds that its combination of power, ease, and affordability makes creativity accessible to everyone.

article_content: It is usually Nessie who makes headlines around Loch Ness — but this past weekend, an earthquake shook the area, felt more than 15 miles away. The 2.4-magnitude tremor originated about a mile south of Drumnadrochit at 8:49 p.m. on Friday, at a depth of 2 kilometers. The British Geological Survey (BGS) confirmed the quake was felt across a wide stretch of the loch and is the latest in a series of recent seismic events in the Highlands. The epicenter lay beneath Loch Ness, and residents in Inverness, Dores, Westhill, Errogie, Brinmore, Farr, Scaniport, Culduthel, Torness, and Inverfarigaig reported feeling the shaking. Some described hearing a deep 'roaring sound' as the ground trembled. One woman from Inverness said, 'I felt the ground shake and heard a roar like thunder. It lasted a few seconds. Who knows — maybe Nessie was just waking up.' Drumnadrochit, located on the northern shore of Loch Ness at the head of Urquhart Bay, is famed as the heart of the Nessie mystery. The village hosts the Loch Ness Centre, Nessieland Castle Monster Centre, and is near Urquhart Castle — long rumored to sit above Nessie’s underwater lair. The quake came just one day after a photograph claimed to be 'the best ever taken of the Loch Ness monster' was revealed as an elaborate hoax by its creator, cruise boat captain George Edwards. Edwards admitted the image was a stunt, saying he had no regrets about his 'bit of fun' — even though it fooled seasoned Nessie hunter Steve Feltham, who has spent two decades searching for the creature. Feltham responded by calling Edwards 'nothing more than a faker and a liar.' The infamous 'Surgeon’s Photograph' from 1934, once thought to show Nessie’s head and neck, was later exposed as a hoax as well. Despite the hoaxes, Loch Ness draws around one million visitors annually, contributing £25 million to the local economy. The UK experiences roughly 200–300 earthquakes each year, but most are too small to notice. About 20–30 exceed magnitude 2.0 and are perceptible over wider areas. The largest recorded onshore earthquake in Scotland occurred near Loch Awe in 1880, measuring 5.2 magnitude. UK earthquakes, especially in northern regions, are commonly linked to glacial rebound: the slow uplift of land previously compressed under massive Ice Age glaciers. Since the ice melted roughly 10,500 years ago, the land has been gradually rising — occasionally triggering tremors.

رات 8:49 بجے درمنڈروچٹ کے تقریباً ایک میل جنوب میں، 2 کلومیٹر کی گہرائی پر مرکوز ہوا۔ برطانوی جیولوجیکل سروے (BGS) نے تصدیق کی کہ زلزلہ لوک کے پورے علاقے میں محسوس کیا گیا اور ہائی لینڈز میں حالیہ سیزمک واقعات کی اس سلسلے کا آخری واقعہ ہے۔ زلزلے کا مرکز لوک نیس کے نیچے تھا، اور انورنس، ڈورس، ویسٹہل، ایروجی، برینمور، فیر، سکینیپورٹ، کلڈوتھل، ٹورنیس اور انورفاریگیئگ کے رہائشیوں نے ہلچل محسوس کی۔ کچھ لوگوں نے زمین کے ہلچل کے ساتھ ایک گہرا 'دھماکہ جیسا آواز' سننا بیان کیا۔ انورنس کی ایک خاتون نے کہا، 'میں نے زمین کے ہلچل اور بجلی کی طرح گرجنے کی آواز محسوس کی۔ یہ کچھ سیکنڈ تک رہا۔ کون جانتا ہے — شاید نیسی صرف ہمیں جگانے آئی تھی۔' درمنڈروچٹ، جو لوک نیس کے شمالی کنارے پر ارکارت بے کے سر پر واقع ہے، نیسی کے راز کا مرکز کہلاتی ہے۔ یہ گاؤں لوک نیس سنٹر، نیسیلینڈ کاسٹل مونسٹر سنٹر کا گھر ہے اور قریب ہی ارکارت کاسٹل واقع ہے — جس کے نیچے نیسی کا کہا جاتا ہے کہ سمندری گھر ہے۔ زلزلہ اس تصویر کے ظاہر ہونے کے ایک دن بعد آیا جسے 'نیسی کی بہترین تصویر' کہا جا رہا تھا، لیکن اس کے مصنف نے اسے ایک جھوٹی چال ثابت کر دیا، جو کرُوز کے کپتان جارج ایڈورڈز تھے۔ ایڈورڈز نے تسلیم کیا کہ یہ ایک مزاح تھا، اور اس نے کہا کہ اس کے 'مذاق' پر اسے کوئی پچھتاوا نہیں — چاہے اس نے دو دہائیوں تک نیسی کی تلاش کرنے والے ماہر سٹیو فیلتھم کو بھی دھوکہ دے دیا ہو۔ فیلتھم نے جواب میں ایڈورڈز کو 'صرف ایک جھوٹا اور جھوٹ بولنے والا' قرار دیا۔ 1934 میں ڈاکٹر رابرت کینیتھ وِلسن نے لی گئی مشہور 'سرجن کی تصویر' جس میں نیسی کے سر اور گردن کو دکھایا گیا تھا، وہ بھی بعد میں جھوٹی ثابت ہو گئی۔ جھوٹوں کے باوجود، لوک نیس سالانہ تقریباً ایک ملین سیاحوں کو اپنی طرف متوجہ کرتا ہے، جو مقامی معیشت کو 25 ملین پاؤنڈ فائدہ پہنچاتا ہے۔ برطانیہ میں سالانہ تقریباً 200–300 زلزلے آتے ہیں، لیکن زیادہ تر بہت چھوٹے ہوتے ہیں کہ کوئی نہیں محسوس کرتا۔ تقریباً 20–30 زلزلے 2.0 سے زیادہ بڑائی کے ہوتے ہیں اور وہ وسیع علاقوں میں محسوس ہوتے ہیں۔ سکاٹ لینڈ میں زمین پر ریکارڈ کیا گیا سب سے بڑا زلزلہ 1880 میں لوک آو کے قریب آیا، جس کی بڑائی 5.2 تھی۔ برطانوی زلزلے، خاص طور پر شمالی علاقوں میں، عام طور پر گلیشیئل ری باؤنڈ کی وجہ سے ہوتے ہیں: وہ زمین جو پرانی برف کی مقدار سے دبی ہوئی تھی، ابھی اس کے پگھلنے کے بعد ابھی تک آہستہ آہستہ اُبھر رہی ہے — جس سے اکثر زلزلے ہوتے ہیں۔

article_content: North Korea’s December 12, 2012 rocket launch has raised serious concerns among South Korean officials, who believe the test demonstrates progress toward developing a missile capable of delivering a warhead over 10,000 kilometers — far enough to reach the U.S. West Coast and parts of Europe. Although Pyongyang claims the Unha-3 rocket successfully placed a weather satellite into orbit, analysts and defense experts argue the launch was primarily a disguised test of long-range ballistic missile technology. South Korea retrieved and analyzed debris from the rocket’s first stage, which fell into the Yellow Sea off its western coast. Examination of components — including what appears to be a fuel tank — suggests the rocket’s propulsion system is more advanced than previously estimated. A South Korean Defense Ministry official stated that based on material analysis, North Korea now possesses the capability to launch a 500–600 kg warhead beyond 10,000 km. This development violates United Nations sanctions imposed after North Korea’s nuclear tests in 2006 and 2009. The UN Security Council condemned the launch shortly after it occurred. While North Korea has historically struggled with failed missile tests, this launch marked a significant technical milestone. Domestically, it bolstered the legitimacy of young leader Kim Jong-un, who assumed power after his father’s death in 2011. In a public address following the launch, Kim Jong-un praised the scientists involved and declared his ambition for ‘a variety of more working satellites’ and ‘carrier rockets of bigger capacity’ — the first explicit endorsement of expanding North Korea’s long-range rocket program. However, experts caution that North Korea remains years away from mastering critical technologies: miniaturizing a nuclear warhead to fit atop a missile, and ensuring the warhead survives atmospheric re-entry without disintegrating. There is currently no confirmed evidence that North Korea has achieved either.

میں میزائل ٹیسٹ میں ناکامیوں کا تجربہ کیا ہے، یہ لانچ ایک اہم ٹیکنیکل اہمیت کا حامل تھا۔ داخلی طور پر، یہ نوجوان لیڈر کِم جونگ اِن کی حکومت کی قانونیت کو مضبوط کرنے میں مدد کیا، جنہوں نے اپنے والد کی والے کیرئیر راکٹس’ چاہتے ہیں — جو شمالی کوریا کے لمبی دُوری راکٹ پروگرام کے توسیع کی پہلی واضح تجویز ہے۔ تاہم، ماہرین کا خیال ہے کہ شمالی کوریا اب بھی اہم ٹیکنالوجیوں میں کامیاب نہیں ہوا ہے: ایٹمی article_content: Could George Clooney’s wedding have sparked a surge in British travelers choosing Venice for their Christmas break? New research reveals a 66% spike in bookings to the Italian city — a trend that coincides with the high-profile marriage of the Hollywood star and human rights lawyer Amal Alamuddin at the luxurious Aman Canal Grande Hotel this autumn. But Venice’s allure isn’t just about celebrity glamour. The city’s enchanting Christmas markets, especially in Campo Santo Stefano, draw crowds with their mouthwatering treats: creamy almond-stuffed nougat, fruit-laden panettone from Verona, and rare white truffles from Alba. These markets offer not just gifts, but a deeply atmospheric holiday experience. According to Andy Washington, Managing Director of Expedia.co.uk, 'The Christmas period is always a peak travel season. Britons flock to both traditional and offbeat Christmas markets across the UK and Europe — and Venice, with its central location, serves as a perfect gateway to explore the Veneto region: Prosecco country, historic villas near Verona, Padua, and Vicenza — all within an hour’s drive.' While London remains the most popular destination for British travelers this Christmas — with bookings up 39% year-on-year — followed by New York and Paris, Venice’s rise stands out. Germany and the Netherlands also saw a 35% increase in festive bookings. London’s Southbank Christmas Market, celebrating the spirit of Charles Dickens this year with a dazzling maze of 300 real blue spruce trees, continues to captivate global visitors. Meanwhile, the Netherlands’ Valkenberg 'Christmas Market Velvet Cave' — nestled beneath the historic Valkenburg Castle — enchants guests with 18th-century sculptures and a cozy, candlelit atmosphere. In Germany, the Royal Christmas Market at Hohenzollern Castle in Stuttgart offers the quintessential Glühwein and bratwurst experience, drawing record numbers. While the ‘Clooney effect’ may add a touch of romance to Venice’s appeal, it’s the city’s timeless beauty, rich traditions, and festive culinary offerings that truly keep visitors coming back.

article_content: Queen Elizabeth II, aged 87, will not travel to Sri Lanka this November for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting — a decision rooted in a broader review of her international travel schedule, according to Buckingham Palace. Instead, her son and heir, Prince Charles, will represent her at the summit in Colombo. Officials clarified that the choice stems from efforts to reduce long-haul flights, not from health concerns — even though the Queen spent a short time in a London hospital earlier this year after being treated for gastroenteritis. Prince Charles, who has long been involved in Commonwealth activities, previously attended the 2007 meeting in Kampala, Uganda. The Commonwealth Secretariat expressed full understanding and appreciation for the Queen’s choice, commending her decades of unwavering commitment to the organization. They also welcomed Charles’s participation, highlighting his enduring ties to the Commonwealth. Comprising 54 independent nations, the Commonwealth represents roughly a quarter of the world’s countries and one-third of its people. These nations convene every two years to foster cooperation on democracy, development, and global challenges. Meetings begin formally but quickly shift into candid, informal discussions where consensus guides all outcomes.

article_content: On the first day of her trial in Hartford Superior Court, 39-year-old Tiffany Stevens faced charges of attempted murder after a convicted felon, John McDaid, testified that she hired him to kill her ex-husband, Eric Stevens, in 2012. The alleged plot emerged amid a bitter child custody dispute involving their young daughter—and a $50 million trust fund contingent on custody. McDaid, who has a decades-long criminal record including 22 felony convictions, said Stevens approached him in April 2012 while he worked as a maintenance worker for a wealthy Simsbury couple. He claimed she handed him an envelope containing $5,000 with the instruction: 'Get it done.' McDaid said he never carried out the plan. Instead, he secretly recorded conversations with Stevens using a computer audio program and informed Eric Stevens, who then contacted police in July 2012. He used the money to buy a washer, dryer, and clothing for his children—while leading Stevens to believe the assassination was imminent. Stevens’ attorneys, Hubert Santos and Trent LaLima, are challenging the authenticity of the audio recording, arguing it may have been tampered with. Judge Edward J. Mullarkey has not yet ruled on its admissibility. Despite the pending criminal case, Stevens remains free on $1 million bail and currently holds physical custody of her daughter. Eric Stevens, meanwhile, says he does not know where his daughter is and is pursuing custody in family court. Simsbury Police Sgt. Gregory Samselski confirmed that Eric Stevens provided the audio recording to authorities, revealing that whoever gained custody of the child would control the substantial trust fund. Stevens, dressed in a black blazer and slacks with her hair in a ponytail, arrived at court accompanied by her father, Edward Khalily, and declined to speak to reporters.

article_content: London, England (CNN) — All non-European immigrants seeking to enter the United Kingdom must now pass a basic English language test to obtain a visa, under new rules announced by the government on Wednesday. The requirement applies to individuals wishing to join a spouse or partner in the UK and will take effect this autumn, according to official statements. Home Secretary Theresa May said, 'I believe being able to speak English should be a prerequisite for anyone who wants to settle here.' She added that the measure will 'help promote integration, remove cultural barriers, and protect public services.' Applicants must demonstrate a basic command of conversational English by passing an approved test at an authorized testing center, the Home Office confirmed. 'It is a privilege to come to the U.K.,' May stated, 'and that is why I am committed to raising the bar for migrants and ensuring those who benefit from being in Britain contribute to our society.' She emphasized that today’s announcement is just the first step, with plans to further strengthen English-language requirements in the future. 'Today’s announcement is part of a broader package of measures the government is implementing to ensure immigration is properly controlled for the benefit of the UK — alongside caps on work visas and a robust system for regulating international students,' May said. Under current regulations, visa applicants joining partners must prove their relationship is genuine and that they can financially support themselves. They initially receive a two-year settlement visa, after which they may apply for indefinite leave to remain — similar to a U.S. green card — by passing a test on British culture, politics, and laws. The new English proficiency test will be required in addition to this existing requirement.
translated_content: لندن، انگلستان (سی این نیوز) — غیر یورپی مہاجرین جو برطانیہ میں داخل ہونا چاہتے ہیں، اب ویزا حاصل کرنے کے لیے بنیادی انگریزی زبان کا امتحان پاس کرنا لازمی ہوگا، جس کا اعلان حکومت نے بدھ کو کیا۔ یہ ضابطہ ان افراد پر لاگو ہوگا جو اپنے شریک حیات سے ملنے برطانیہ آنا چاہتے ہیں، اور یہ نئے قوانین اس سال خزانہ کے موسم میں نافذ ہوں گے، جیسا کہ سرکاری بیانات میں کہا گیا۔ وزیرِ داخلہ تھیریزا مے نے کہا، 'مجھے یقین ہے کہ یہاں بسنا چاہنے والے کسی بھی شخص کے لیے انگریزی بولنا ایک شرط ہونی چاہیے۔' انہوں نے کہا کہ یہ اقدام 'ایکیجیشن کو فروغ دے گا، ثقافتی رکاوٹوں کو ختم کرے گا، اور عوامی خدمات کا تحفظ کرے گا۔' درخواست گزاروں کو ایک منظور شدہ ٹیسٹ مرکز میں بنیادی گفتگو کی انگریزی کی صلاحیت ثابت کرنا ہوگی، جیسا کہ ہوم آفس نے تصدیق کی۔ مے نے کہا، 'برطانیہ میں آنا ایک خصوصی عطا ہے، اور اسی لیے میں مہاجروں کے لیے معیار بلند کرنے اور اس بات کو یقینی بنانے کے لیے متعهد ہوں کہ جو لوگ برطانیہ میں فائدہ اٹھا رہے ہیں وہ ہماری معاشرے میں حصہ ڈالیں۔' انہوں نے زور دے کر کہا کہ آج کا اعلان صرف پہلا قدم ہے، اور مستقبل میں انگریزی زبان کی درخواستوں کو مزید سخت کرنے کی منصوبہ بندی ہے۔ مے نے کہا، 'آج کا اعلان حکومت کی ایک وسیع سیریز اقدامات کا حصہ ہے جو مہاجرت کو برطانیہ کے فائدے کے لیے درست طریقے سے کنٹرول کرنے کے لیے کیے جا رہے ہیں — جن میں کام کے ویزوں پر پابندی اور بین الاقوامی طلبہ کے لیے مضبوط نظام شامل ہیں۔' موجودہ ضوابط کے تحت، شریک حیات کے ساتھ جڑنے کے لیے درخواست دینے والوں کو اپنے شادی شدہ تعلقات کی اصلیت اور مالی طور پر خود کو سنبھالنے کی صلاحیت ثابت کرنا ہوتی ہے۔ وہ ابتدا میں دو سالہ سیٹلمنٹ ویزا حاصل کرتے ہیں، اس کے بعد وہ 'انڈیفنٹ لیو ٹو ریمن' کے لیے درخواست دے سکتے ہیں — جو امریکہ کی گرین کارڈ کے برابر ہے — لیکن اس کے لیے انہیں برطانیہ کی ثقافت، سیاست اور قانونوں پر امتحان پاس کرنا ہوتا ہے۔ نیا انگریزی امتحان اس موجودہ امتحان کے علاوہ لازمی ہوگا۔

article_content: A Milwaukee woman was charged with drunk driving after being caught riding a motorcycle with no hands on Friday afternoon. Police observed her driving past them with an unzipped jacket and no clothing underneath, screaming at passing vehicles. Dashcam footage from the patrol car shows her adopting a Christ-like pose on the motorcycle as she weaved erratically through traffic. A deputy can be heard saying, 'She's screaming at every car on the freeway and kind of assaulting people with her motorcycle.' Officers pursued her for several miles northbound on Interstate 43, where she traveled at 57 miles per hour. The Bayside Police Department requested backup to manage traffic as she swerved unpredictably across lanes, showing little regard for safety. At one point, she slowed to 10 mph in a 65 mph zone, then accelerated again after readjusting her position. The pursuit ended when she lost control of the motorcycle in the middle of the highway. Police rushed to assist her. She was described as 'clearly out of it' and stammering about religion. Miraculously, her only injury was a cut on her chin. In addition to exceeding the legal blood alcohol limit, police suspect she was under the influence of prescription drugs. This marks her second arrest for drunk driving.

article_content: A flyer advertising drinks at 80p each at Electric nightclub in Birmingham sparked outrage, with critics labeling the promotion 'utterly irresponsible.' The event, dubbed 'Twisted Monday,' was intended to coincide with the end of university exams and promised to be 'Birmingham’s Biggest Monday Night.' Former Health Minister Gisela Stuart, Labour MP for Edgbaston, condemned the plan, stating, 'It’s utterly irresponsible to encourage cheap, heavy drinking on a Monday night. We already have overloaded A&Es—we don’t need more alcohol-related emergencies.' Debbie Bannigan, Chief Executive of the alcohol charity Swanswell, emphasized that responsibility lies not only with consumers but also with venues selling alcohol. Katherine Brown of the Institute of Alcohol Studies added that cheap alcohol availability fuels nationwide harms, often leaving public servants to clean up the consequences. Tickets for the event were advertised at £4. Birmingham City Council, responsible for licensing, stated the event did not violate Home Office guidelines on responsible drinking. Following widespread criticism, the event—scheduled for February 2—was canceled. Ray Mohamed, a freelance promoter for GLM, claimed the venue would have enforced responsible service: 'If staff see someone overly intoxicated, they won’t serve them anymore. The 80p offer was just a draw to bring people in.' Electric’s manager, Amo Taib, denied the cancellation was due to ethical concerns, saying the event was never officially confirmed and was 'not cost-effective.' He added that promoters had prematurely advertised the night before it was finalized. 'As a company and as a club, it’s not something I wanted to do. It was only ever in talks.' GLM has not yet responded to requests for comment.

article_content: (CNN) -- Formula One supremo Bernie Ecclestone has dismissed reports that CVC Capital Partners, the sport’s owner, may be preparing to sell. According to Sky News — owned by Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp — media mogul Rupert Murdoch and Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim are lining up a bid. But the 80-year-old Ecclestone, who has managed F1 on behalf of CVC since selling his rights to the private equity firm in 2006, said such a sale would not serve the commercial interests of the sport. 'Formula One is not for sale. And anyway, we would not sell to a media company because it would restrict our ability to negotiate with other broadcasters,' he told Britain’s The Times on Wednesday. Ecclestone, who first secured the rights to negotiate television contracts for F1 races in the late 1970s, added that News Corp had not approached CVC. 'If they were interested, they would have called me — and they haven’t,' he told Bloomberg. 'If someone came along with an offer far exceeding its value, then obviously they’d have to consider it. But they’ve never even discussed selling.' The current Concorde Agreement between F1 teams expires next year. Ferrari, one of eight teams on the grid that attempted a failed breakaway in 2009 before signing the agreement, is reportedly among those seeking to wrest control from Ecclestone. Meanwhile, the British entrepreneur is assisting German prosecutors investigating Gerhard Gribkowsky, a former executive at state-owned BayernLB, which held a stake in F1 until 2006. Gribkowsky has been arrested on suspicion of fraud related to the 2006 sale. 'I have been cooperating with the State Prosecution Office’s investigation into Dr. Gribkowsky’s affairs from the outset,' Ecclestone said in a statement last week. 'When I learned there were initial suspicions regarding my involvement, I visited the Senior State Prosecutor and her team in Munich earlier this month to clarify any allegations. I am confident that once all the facts are established, I will be fully exonerated.'
translated_content: (CNN) -- فارمولا ون کے سپریمو بیرنی ایکلستون نے اس بات کی اطلاعات مسترد کر دیں کہ کے وی سی کیپٹل پارٹنرز، جو کھیل کے مالک ہیں، فروخت کرنے کا ارادہ رکھتے ہیں۔ اس کی اطلاع سکائی نیوز نے دی، جو رپرٹ مرڈوک کے نیوز کارپ کی ملکیت ہے، جس میں میڈیا مگنیٹ رپرٹ مرڈوک اور میکسیکن اربپتی کارلوس سلم کی طرف سے نیا آفر ہونے کی اطلاع ہے۔ لیکن 80 سالہ ایکلستون، جو 2006 میں اپنے حقوق کے فروخت کے بعد سی وی سی کی طرف سے فارمولا ون کا انتظام کر رہے ہیں، نے کہا کہ ایسا کاروبار کھیل کے تجارتی مفاد کے خلاف ہوگا۔ 'فارمولا ون فروخت کے لیے نہیں ہے۔ اور بالاخر، ہم کسی میڈیا کمپنی کو نہیں بیچیں گے کیونکہ یہ دیگر پریس کے ساتھ مذاکرات کی صلاحیت کو محدود کر دے گا،' انہوں نے ہفتے کو برطانیہ کے ٹائمز کو بتایا۔ ایکلستون، جنہوں نے 1970 کی دہائی کے آخر میں فارمولا ون کے مقابلے کے لیے ٹیلی ویژن معاہدے کے لیے حقوق حاصل کیے تھے، نے کہا کہ نیوز کارپ نے سی وی سی سے رابطہ نہیں کیا۔ 'اگر ان کی دلچسپی ہوتی تو وہ میرے ساتھ فون کرتے — اور انہوں نے نہیں کیا،' انہوں نے بلومبرگ کو بتایا۔ 'اگر کوئی اتنا بڑا آفر لے کر آئے جو اس کی قیمت سے کہیں زیادہ ہو، تو انہیں اس پر غور کرنا ہوگا۔ لیکن انہوں نے کبھی فروخت کے بارے میں بات بھی نہیں کی۔' فارمولا ون ٹیموں کے درمیان موجود کنکورڈ معاہدہ اگلے سال ختم ہو رہا ہے۔ article_content: An iconic American civil rights group originally founded to combat the Ku Klux Klan has now placed renowned African-American neurosurgeon and potential 2016 presidential candidate Ben Carson on its 'Extremist Watch' list—for opposing same-sex marriage. Carson, a retired pediatric neurosurgeon known for his humanitarian work, called the classification 'projectionist and ignorant,' adding, 'Oh, definitely [the SPLC is crooked].' He questioned how an organization that fights hate could label someone whose life’s work saved children as a 'hater.' Carson highlighted his scholarship programs and literacy initiatives in underserved communities, stating, 'Because I don’t agree with them about traditional marriage, I’m labeled a “hater.” That’s pretty interesting.' His controversial remarks—including comparing Obamacare to slavery and suggesting same-sex marriage could lead to societal collapse akin to the fall of Rome—have drawn sharp criticism. He later apologized on CNN, saying his comments were 'somewhat insensitive' and affirming, 'I love gay people. I love straight people.' The SPLC, which lists Carson alongside neo-Nazis and former Klan leaders, justifies its inclusion by citing his association with groups that oppose LGBTQ+ rights and his use of inflammatory language, such as referencing NAMBLA in discussions about marriage. The SPLC’s practice of publishing extremist lists has been linked to real violence: In 2012, gunman Floyd Corkins attacked the Family Research Council after using the SPLC’s 'Hate Map' to identify targets. Critics, including legal scholars, argue the SPLC has drifted from its original mission, becoming a politically partisan entity. Its funding sources—including donations from Jeffry Picower, a key beneficiary of Bernie Madoff’s fraud—further fuel skepticism. Despite Carson’s apologies and affirmations of equality, the SPLC has not responded to repeated requests for comment. Its spokesperson, Mark Potok, defended the listing, arguing that Carson’s rhetoric promotes intolerance under the guise of religious belief.

ہوں۔' SPLC، جو کارسن کو نیو نازیز اور سابقہ کلینسمن کے ساتھ فہرست میں شامل کرتی ہے، اس کی وجہ ان کے ہم جنس پرستی کے خلاف گروہوں کے ساتھ تعلق اور ایسے الفاظ کا استعمال بتاتی ہے جیسے کہ شادی کے بارے میں article_content: On New Year’s Day in Victoria Park, East London, a Tower Hamlets Enforcement Officer called for police backup after accusing Amber Langtry, 35, of failing to clean up after her German Shepherd, Olive. Langtry, walking with a friend who recorded the encounter, denied the claim, insisting her dog had not been near the feces. Despite this, she voluntarily picked up the waste to de-escalate the situation. The officer issued a notice that could lead to a £1,000 fine and a court hearing, citing 'non-compliance' — referring to Langtry’s refusal to provide her name. He also described Langtry’s friend as 'aggressive' for filming the exchange. For nearly ten minutes, Langtry repeatedly asked the officer to show her the alleged feces — a request he initially refused. When police arrived, they expressed confusion, noting no criminal allegation had been made. After about half an hour, the officer finally pointed out the waste, which Langtry maintained was not from her dog. Still, she disposed of it responsibly. In a five-page letter, Tower Hamlets Council later confirmed it would not pursue prosecution. However, it reiterated its policy of enforcing dog fouling laws and defended the officer’s decision to call for backup after Langtry declined to provide her name. Langtry told the Evening Standard and Mail Online that while the incident now seems absurd — 'Why did he need police backup for a five-foot-four woman looking for dog poo?' — it was at the time 'scary, intimidating, and confusing.' The Metropolitan Police confirmed no crime was reported. The council stands by its zero-tolerance approach to dog faeces, citing resident concerns.

article_content: Although Hillary Clinton has publicly stated she isn’t considering a 2016 presidential run—and even asked supporters not to speculate—her allies are quietly building the entire machinery of a campaign anyway. A coalition of major Democratic organizations, including Priorities USA Action, Ready for Hillary, Emily’s List, and Correct the Record, are operating with remarkable synchronicity, each handling distinct but complementary tasks: fundraising, grassroots mobilization, messaging, and rapid-response defense. What makes this unusual is how tightly knit these groups are. Their leadership overlaps heavily: board members of Priorities USA Action include key figures from all the other pro-Clinton outfits, many of whom have worked together for decades. Former Obama campaign manager Jim Messina joining as co-chair only deepened speculation—even though the White House insisted he’s acting independently. These aren’t random connections. Staffers from different groups regularly meet over lunch, share weekly calls, and alert each other about events. Trust built over years of campaigning means communication flows smoothly—and often informally. As one insider put it, 'The line between work drinks and Friday night drinks is blurry.' Still, not everyone is cheering. Senior Democrats warn that fixating on 2016 risks neglecting the urgent 2014 midterms, where control of the Senate hangs in the balance. Guy Cecil of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee urged donors to stay focused on protecting blue seats, while David Axelrod questioned why money wasn’t being directed toward stopping Republican super PACs now. In response, pro-Clinton groups insist they’re not ignoring 2014. Priorities USA Action has pledged active involvement in midterm races, arguing that preserving Obama’s legacy depends on winning them. But the reality remains: every dollar raised, every email collected, every strategy drafted is aimed squarely at a potential Clinton run. And if she doesn’t run? The groups say they’ll redirect resources to other Democrats—but no one truly believes that’s the plan. The infrastructure exists because Clinton is the presumed nominee. A recent poll shows 70% of Democrats would back her, and even critics concede she’s the overwhelming favorite. There’s a bitter twist: these very groups once condemned the Citizens United decision that unleashed unlimited corporate spending in politics. Now, they’re using it to their advantage. 'We can’t unilaterally disarm,' says one strategist. In the new political landscape, playing by the rules—even if you hate them—is the only way to compete.

ملتے ہیں، ہفتہ وار کالز پر بات چیت کرتے ہیں، اور ایک دوسرے کو ایونٹس کے بارے میں آگاہ کرتے ہیں۔ سالوں کے سیاست کے تجربے نے اعتماد قائم کیا ہے، جس کی وجہ سے رابطہ آسان ہوتا ہے—اور اکثر غیر رسمی طور پر۔ article_content: Allen Stanford, a Texan tycoon once worth over £1.2 billion, was sentenced to 110 years in prison for orchestrating a £5 billion investment fraud that victimized an estimated 17,000 to 28,000 people. Many of those affected were small business owners and private investors drawn in by promises of unusually high returns on certificates of deposit issued by his Antigua-based bank. For over two decades, Stanford built a global financial empire — and a larger-than-life public image — fueled by investor funds. He lavished money on luxury yachts, private jets, and high-profile cricket sponsorships in England, including the controversial Stanford 20/20 Super Series in 2008, where he famously posed with England players and was photographed bouncing the wife of cricketer Matt Prior on his knee. Convicted in March on 13 of 14 fraud charges, Stanford stood before a packed Houston courtroom where victims spoke out. Jaime Escalona, representing Latin American claimants, called him 'a dirty, rotten, scoundrel.' Angela Shaw of the Stanford Victims Coalition said he 'took our lives as we knew them.' Yet even as he faced justice, Stanford refused to accept responsibility. 'I did not defraud anybody,' he insisted, blaming the U.S. government and a court-appointed receiver for destroying his business. He claimed his operations were legitimate and that he was made a scapegoat. Prosecutors described him as a 'ruthless predator' who treated victims like 'roadkill.' They sought a 230-year sentence, arguing it wouldn't restore lost money but would ensure he spent his life reflecting on his crimes. Stanford’s empire collapsed in 2009 when regulators shut down his operations. Since then, authorities have frozen £212 million in assets held in bank accounts across London, Canada, and Switzerland. Three former executives await trial, and a former Antiguan regulator has been indicted for extradition to the U.S. Despite being declared legally indigent — meaning he has no assets — the court will assign federally funded lawyers to handle his appeal. His final words in court were defiant: 'If I live the rest of my life in prison, I will always be at peace with the way I conducted myself in business.' His fraud ranks as the second-largest in U.S. history, surpassed only by Bernie Madoff’s £11.2 billion scheme. The UK’s England and Wales Cricket Board severed ties with him in 2009, stripping his honorary knighthood from Antigua. Reporters noted that while Stanford portrayed himself as a savior of English cricket, he admitted he never truly understood the game.

17,000 و28,000 شخص. وكان العديد من الضحايا من أصحاب الأعمال الصغيرة والمستثمرين الخاصين الذين جذبهم وعود بعوائد غير عادية على شهادات الإيداع الصادرة من بنكه في أنتيغوا. على مدار عقدين، بنى ستانفورد إمبراطورية مالية عالمية — وصورة عامة ضخمة — مموّلة بأموال المستثمرين. أنفق أموالاً طائلة على يخوت فاخرة، وأسطول من الطائرات الخاصة، ورعاية رياضية بارزة في إنجلترا، بما في ذلك سلسلة ستانفورد 20/20 المثيرة للجدل عام 2008، حيث ظهر وهو يلتقط صورًا مع لاعبي إنجلترا، وصُور وهو يجلس على ركبته ويرفرف بزوجة اللاعب مات بريور. بعد إدانته في مارس على 13 من أصل 14 تهم احتيال، وقف ستانفورد أمام محكمة هيوستن المكتظة، حيث تحدث الضحايا. وقال خافيير إسكالونا، الممثل عن الضحايا اللاتينيين: 'أنت وحش قذر ومخادع.' وقالت أنجيلا شاو من تحالف ضحايا ستانفورد: 'لقد سرق حياتنا كما عرفناها.' لكن حتى في لحظة العدالة، رفض ستانفورد تقبّل المسؤولية. قال: 'لم أخدع أحدًا'، وألقى اللوم على الحكومة الأمريكية ومُستلم المحكمة المعيّن لإتلاف عمله. وأكد أن عملياته كانت مشروعة وأنه أصبح كبش فداء. وصف المدعون العامون ستانفورد بأنه 'مفترس لا رحمة له' تعامل مع الضحايا كـ'مُهملين'. وطلبوا حكمًا بالسجن 230 سنة، قائلين إنه لن يعيد الأموال المفقودة، لكنه سيضمن أن يقضي حياته يفكر في ما فعله. انهارت إمبراطورية ستانفورد في 2009 عندما أغلقت الجهات التنظيمية عملياته. ومنذ ذلك الحين، تم تجميد 212 مليون جنيه إسترليني من الأصول المودعة في حسابات مصرفية بلندن وكندا وسويسرا. وينتظر ثلاثة مديرين سابقين محاكمتهم، كما وجهت تهمة إلى منظم مالي سابق في أنتيغوا واستُدعي لتسليم نفسه للولايات المتحدة. على الرغم من إعلانه رسميًا كشخص بلا أصول — أي أنه لا يملك شيئًا — فستعين المحكمة محامين ممولين من قبل الدولة للتعامل مع استئنافه. وكانت كلماته الأخيرة في المحكمة متحدية: 'إذا عشت باقي حياتي في السجن، فسأظل دائمًا مرتاحًا مع الطريقة التي قمت بها بأعمالي التجارية.' يصنّف احتياله كثاني أكبر عملية احتيال في التاريخ الأمريكي، ويتفوق عليه فقط احتيال برنارد مادوف بقيمة 11.2 مليار جنيه إسترليني. قطعت هيئة كريكيت إنجلترا وويلز علاقتها به في 2009، وألغت لقبه الفخري من أنتيغوا. لاحظ المحررون أنه بينما صوّر ستانفورد نفسه كمنقذ للكريكيت الإنجليزي، إلا أنه اعترف بأنه لم يفهم اللعبة حقًا.
